titulo: Review and test of the first block: The most common mistakes

aula.titulo: Review and test of the first block
aula.objetivo: Review pronunciation, articles, the present tense, the accusative, separable verbs, time and directions, correct the most common mistakes of English speakers and take the test of the first block.

blocos.titulo: The 10 most common mistakes of English speakers
blocos.explicacao: These ten mistakes appear most often in English speakers. Correcting only these already makes your German much more natural. Read each pair out loud: first the wrong one (to recognise the strange sound), then the right one.

erros.motivo: Learn the article together with the word.
Capital letter at the start of the sentence and on every noun.
The second verb goes to the end.

erros.certo: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.

itens.ru: Wie heißt du? / Wie heißen Sie?
itens.translit: vee hyst doo / vee HEYE-sen zee
itens.audio: Wie heißt du? / Wie heißen Sie?

itens.explicacao: Wo asks for the place where someone lives: Wo wohnst du? Wohin asks for a destination and woher for an origin.

itens.enunciado: Ask for the destination: ___ gehst du heute?
itens.explicacao: The prompt asks for the destination. Wohin means where to: Wohin gehst du heute? Without this context, other questions with gehen could also be possible.

itens.enunciado: Ask for the origin: ___ kommt Tom?
itens.explicacao: The prompt asks for the origin. Woher means where from: Woher kommt Tom? Wohin would ask for the destination, not the origin requested.
The prompt says the answer is a person. Wer is used to ask who someone is: Wer ist das?
To ask about an activity, was is used: Was machst du heute? Wer asks about a person, not about an action.

itens.enunciado: Which of the three is a yes/no question?
itens.explicacao: Wohnst du hier? is a yes/no question: the conjugated verb comes before the subject. The other options start with question words and ask for specific information.

itens.enunciado: Fill in the questions by conjugating the verb: ___ du Deutsch? (lernen) · Wo wohnt Camila? (wohnen)
itens.explicacao: With du, lernen becomes lernst. In a yes/no question, the conjugated verb opens the sentence: Lernst du Deutsch?

itens.enunciado: Fill in the questions by conjugating the verb: Lernst du Deutsch? (lernen) · Wo ___ Camila? (wohnen)
itens.explicacao: Camila corresponds to the third person singular; wohnen becomes wohnt. In the question with Wo, the verb comes after the question word: Wo wohnt Camila?

itens.enunciado: Fill in the questions by conjugating the verb: Woher ___ ihr? (kommen) · Wohnen Sie in München? (wohnen)
itens.explicacao: With ihr, kommen becomes kommt. After Woher, the order verb and subject is kept: Woher kommt ihr?

itens.enunciado: Fill in the questions by conjugating the verb: Woher kommt ihr? (kommen) · ___ Sie in München? (wohnen)
itens.explicacao: With the formal Sie, wohnen has the form wohnen. Since the yes/no question starts with the verb, you write Wohnen Sie in München?

itens.enunciado: Turn into a yes/no question in the order verb–subject–time: Tom arbeitet heute. → ___
itens.explicacao: For the yes/no question in the requested order, put the conjugated verb before the subject and keep heute at the end: Arbeitet Tom heute?

itens.enunciado: Match each question with the right answer: (1) Wer ist das? · (2) Was machst du? · (3) Wie alt bist du? · (4) Woher kommst du? · (5) Wo wohnst du? Answers: (a) In Schwabing. · (b) Ich bin 28 Jahre alt. · (c) Das ist Jonas. · (d) Aus Brasilien. · (e) Ich lerne Deutsch.

blocos.enunciado: Read each mistake out loud and say the right form. Then record 5 sentences of your own, without any of these mistakes.
Write 3 mistakes you have already made in German and the right form.
